findings.title: Denial cache key is ambiguous: name and parent are joined with "_" and both can contain "_"
findings.body: `userPermDenialCacheKey` builds `ns.perm_<uid>_<action>_<name>_<parent>` by plain concatenation. `name` and `parent` come straight from `req.GetName()` and `req.GetFolder()` (service.go:226-227), and Grafana UIDs can contain `_`. Two different requests can therefore produce the same key. For example, `name="a_b", folder="c"` and `name="a", folder="b_c"` both give `..._a_b_c`. Once one of them is denied, `Check` (service.go:117) returns `Allowed:false` for the other for up to 30s. It does this before any permission lookup, and nothing logs it. The result is a silent wrong denial for a resource the user may have access to. Use an unambiguous encoding, such as a separator that cannot appear in a UID, length-prefixing, or hashing the tuple. Also consider a distinct prefix such as `.perm_denied_`, so the key can never share a namespace with `userPermCacheKey` in the same underlying cache.

findings.title: Deny-entry test comment contradicts the data it sets up, and the allow side is never exercised
findings.body: The comment says "Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked", but the permCache entry is `{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false}`, which is not an allow. The test therefore does not prove the denial entry takes precedence over cached allow permissions. Set the value to `true`, which is what `getScopeMap` would produce for a granted permission, so the test fails if the denial lookup is moved after the permission lookup. Also, nothing tests that a denial is written after a DB-backed deny (`permDenialCache.Set` at service.go:154), or that the key is isolated per name and folder. There is also no cached-path test for the anonymous identity type in `getCachedIdentityPermissions`.

findings.title: In-process client now has no client-side cache; each Check decodes the user's whole permission map from JSON
findings.body: The in-process client previously used a 30s local cache of check results (the removed `newRBACClient`). It now uses `NoopCache`, so every Check reaches `Service.Check`. `getCachedIdentityPermissions` then does `json.Unmarshal` of the user's entire scope map (cache.go:70) before `checkPermission` runs. For users with many permissions this is per-request CPU and allocation that was previously avoided on repeated identical checks. Please confirm this was measured. Also, `NoopCache` is an exported type in package `authz` with no other users in `pkg` (grep). Unexport it, or use an existing no-op cache if authlib has one.

contracts.action: Check consults a per-(user,action,name,folder) denial cache, then the cached permission map, before falling back to the DB path
contracts.equivalent_path: Previously getUserPermissions/getAnonymousPermissions read permCache themselves and then ran checkPermission; the client-side authlib cache (30s) fronted the in-process service.
contracts.before_after: Before: the cache read lived inside getUserPermissions (removed at service.go:379) and a cached map was always used for the decision. After: a cached map that does not allow the request falls through to the DB (service.go:131-139), and a DB-backed deny is cached for shortCacheTTL (service.go:153-155). The cache hit and miss metrics are moved up into Check and List.
contracts.visible_effect: A deny is served from cache for up to 30s even if the permission is granted in the meantime. Same staleness bound as permCache (shortCacheTTL=30s, service.go:32).
contracts.failure_mode: The denial key can collide across different name/folder pairs (cache.go:31), which gives a silent wrong deny. Cache Get/Set failures are only logged and fall through to the DB (cache.go:65-90).

contracts.action: List reads cached permissions first and falls back to getIdentityPermissions
contracts.before_after: Before: a single getIdentityPermissions call, with the cache check inside. After: the cache is checked first (errors are swallowed) and the DB path runs on any error. getUserPermissions no longer rechecks the cache inside singleflight (service.go:379-380). Concurrent misses are still coalesced by sf.Do.
contracts.visible_effect: The same List results; the cache metric is now emitted in List.
contracts.failure_mode: If GetUserIdentifiers fails in the cached path, the error is swallowed and retried in the DB path, which returns the error (service.go:186-191). Nothing is lost.

summary: The caching restructure in `Check` and `List` is sound in outline. The main defect is the denial cache key (`pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go:31`). It joins free-form `name` and `folder` strings with `_`, so different resources can share a key and get a silent, cached wrong denial. The deny-entry test also sets a `false` value where its comment says it grants access. Dropping the in-process client cache (`NoopCache`) shifts per-check JSON decoding of the whole permission map onto the service, which is worth confirming.
